Theme 076 · Characters & mascots

Sticker Cast

Everything is a die-cut vinyl sticker slapped onto a mint backdrop: emoji-style faces, chart stickers, lettering with fat white borders. Pulse is a one-eyed teal sticker creature that keeps its eye on the metrics while the emoji cast reacts.

readability ●●●trust ●●○effort low
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

Dashboard stickers slap on one per 8th note, piling up from the bottom until the tired face lands last with a wobble; the headline sticker peels down from the top on the 0:04 snare.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

The mark sticker slams down on the drop (scale 1.3→1, 0.12 s, with a 4-frame squash) and the page shakes 6 px; ‘Acme Pulse’ lettering slaps on beat 2, the Pulse eye on beat 3.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

The anomaly card slaps on beat 1, the −18% flips in, the shocked face lands a beat later with a squash. Pulse’s eye darts to the card, the hand sticker slides in from the right and taps Roll back on the next downbeat.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

The sticker sheet slides up, the taglines peel off and re-stick one beat apart, and Start free lands on the final hit with a tiny rotation overshoot.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Die-cut sticker — any element with a fat white border and soft drop shadow
  • Pulse eye — teal one-eyed sticker creature with the coral dot; the watcher
  • Emoji reactions — tired → shocked → happy faces carry the emotional beat
  • Chart stickers — mini dashboards, overlapping and rotated = overload
  • Die-cut lettering — headlines with a thick white stroke outline
  • Sticker sheet — backing paper with kiss-cut outlines for the CTA

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Slap-on — scale 1.25→1 with rotation settle, 0.12 s expo.out + 0.2 s elastic wobble; every slap sits on an 8th or quarter note
  • Peel & re-stick — corner curl via a rotating triangle mask, 0.3 s power2.inOut, released on the backbeat
  • Eye dart — Pulse’s iris snaps to its target in 0.08 s power4.out, 1 beat before the thing it looks at reacts

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: Stickers and emoji are the native language of team chat, where anomaly alerts actually land; the cast turns a monitoring story into a 3-second emotional arc (tired → shocked → relieved) with zero reading. Risk: Can tip into ‘meme’ and undercut trust — keep one real data card crisp and unrotated enough to read, and limit the cast to 3 characters.

Adapt to your product: Die-cut your own UI cards, logo and one mascot as stickers, pick 3 emoji-style reactions for your before/during/after, and make your CTA the last sticker on the sheet.

References: https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-emoji (open-source (MIT) emoji faces for flat/3D reaction styles) · https://telegram.org/blog/animated-stickers (Lottie-based animated stickers at 60 fps: the motion language of chat)
